packages.title: DESNZ UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics, 2005 to 2024 — scope and status QA
facts: DESNZ published the 2005 to 2024 UK local and regional greenhouse-gas emissions release on 25 June 2026 and added web-accessible documents on 30 June 2026.
The release provides UK local-authority and regional greenhouse-gas estimates using nationally available datasets.
The series can be filtered by sector and covers changes across the time series from 2005.
Local-authority estimates are territorial geographic statistics and are not measurements for individual land parcels.
No parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred from local-authority totals.

packages.title: DESNZ UK local authority and regional greenhouse gas emissions statistics collection — scope and status QA
facts: DESNZ last updated the local-authority and regional greenhouse-gas statistics collection on 25 June 2026.
The collection describes these estimates as the most reliable and consistent national-data breakdown of greenhouse-gas emissions across the country.
The collection covers territorial carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide emissions, while fluorinated gases are not included in this local series.
The local series is intended for local and regional indicators and inventories rather than parcel-level attribution.
Collection scope must be preserved when comparing it with the broader UK territorial inventory.

Final national territorial statistics are not parcel-level greenhouse-gas measurements.

packages.title: DESNZ 2025 UK greenhouse gas emissions provisional statistical release — scope and status QA
facts: The DESNZ 2025 greenhouse-gas estimates are explicitly provisional.
In the provisional release, domestic transport accounted for 31% of UK emissions in 2025.
The domestic-transport sector includes road vehicles, domestic aviation and shipping, fishing vessels and railways, but excludes international aviation and shipping.
The release reports domestic-transport emissions increased by 2% between 2024 and 2025.
Provisional sector estimates must not be presented as final or converted directly into parcel emissions.

packages.title: ONS Energy use: total — scope and status QA
facts: ONS released the current Energy use: total dataset on 5 June 2026.
The dataset covers direct UK energy use from fossil fuels and other sources from 1990 to 2024.
It includes nuclear, net imports, renewables, biofuels and waste alongside reallocated industry energy use.
ONS notes that statistical series can be revised as additional data or methodological changes become available.
Energy-use activity is not itself a parcel greenhouse-gas measurement.

packages.title: ONS Energy use: by industry, source and fuel — scope and status QA
facts: ONS released the current Energy use by industry, source and fuel dataset on 5 June 2026.
The dataset covers 1990 to 2024 across around 130 SIC industry groups, around 80 activity sources and around 20 fuels.
Activity sources include industrial combustion, domestic combustion, aircraft and road transport.
Fuel-use activity and greenhouse-gas emissions must remain distinct unless an explicit accepted conversion model is applied.
No parcel greenhouse-gas value is inferred from the energy-use table.

packages.title: DfT Transport energy and environment data tables (ENV) — scope and status QA
facts: DfT last updated the ENV transport energy and environment tables on 14 July 2026.
The tables cover fuel consumption, greenhouse-gas emissions, pollutants and emissions from journeys.
Coverage periods differ between tables because each table uses the most recently available data sources.
The petroleum-consumption modal breakdown is no longer included in ENV0101 and is referenced to DESNZ energy-consumption tables.
ENV table values do not establish parcel-level emissions.
